BiblicalUsage: Gazal is robbery, the taking of what belongs to another by force. The people of the land have used oppression and exercised robbery in Ezekiel 22:29, and the LORD says He hates robbery for burnt offering in Isaiah 61:8. A soul that takes a thing away by violence has committed a trespass in Leviticus 6:2, and the psalmist warns not to become vain in robbery in Psalms 62:10.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God hates robbery most when it is dressed up as worship. A burnt offering bought with stolen goods is an abomination, and I hold that the only offering God accepts is the one that comes from honest hands.
